comments.text:
I don't understand why you don't just slightly dampen the leather where the fold goes.
When it's slightly damp, it bends much more easily without putting stress on the fibers.
I don't understand why you burnish the edge first and only then dye it.
If you dye it first, the dye penetrates the fibers better; the way you're doing it—dyeing after the fibers have been fully compressed—results in just a surface coating that won't last very long, especially since you're applying dye over another chemical treatment.
comments.author: leatheraccessories646

comments.text: Shell cordovan doesn’t react well with water as it’s a membrane and not skin. The dye afterwards does penetrate and leaves a lighter finish. I didn’t want it to be too dark.
